bullets.text: Nomura initiates India aluminium: prefers VAML, then Hindalco, then NALCO; deck of LME $3,200/t FY27F falling to $2,900/t FY29F vs $3,000-3,100 spot.
bullets.source: Nomura — Anchor Report: India Aluminum - Beyond war premium

detail.summary: Nomura argues aluminium and alumina are decoupling, and that spot embeds an unsustainable war risk premium as Gulf and Indonesian supply returns. With flat-to-falling prices, it says EBITDA growth must come from volume, cost and mix, favouring integrated names over pure smelters.
points: LME aluminium +20% in 2026, $3,850/t peak in June
VAML net leverage 1.44x, declining; Sijimali and Kuraloi mines ramping
NALCO cheapest on spot, but smelter expansion delayed to FY30-31
Guinea targeting exports of ~150MT from ~200MT
Hindalco diversified via Novelis and India downstream

points: Balance: -0.3mt 2026E to +0.9mt 2027E
China price forecast down 9% to Rmb21,500/t

bullets.source: Aditya Birla Money — Initiating Coverage | Steel: Addressing key investor debates; Prefer JSW Steel, ArcelorMittal, and SAIL

detail.summary: Argues the global steel cycle is strengthening as protectionism breaks import-parity pricing and allows regional price discovery. Inventory drawdown, demand outpacing supply
ArcelorMittal covered with positive view

bullets.text: RBI MPC minutes: unanimous 25bp hike to 5.50% but two dissents on stance; Emkay and Kotak both see 25bp more in Dec and Feb.

detail.summary: The unanimous vote hides disagreement on duration: only four of six backed 'calibrated tightening', while Nagesh Kumar and Ram Singh wanted neutral, Singh warning against a higher-for-longer cycle. Emkay reads a high bar for extending beyond measured hikes; Kotak stresses pre-emption against second-round effects.

bullets.text: CLSA: India-US 10-year spread has halved to 2-2.5pp as US 10Y hit 5.30% and India's 7.4%; INR stays the pressure valve.
bullets.source: CLSA — India economics: Mr. Bond is back

detail.summary: CLSA attributes the narrowing to diverging fiscal paths: US deficits and front-loaded maturities against Indian consolidation and longer tenor. Higher commodity prices hit India's inflation harder. It argues policymakers face a choice between defending INR and domestic rate control, and favours a market-determined currency.
points: US 10Y 5.30%, up over 1pp YTD; India 10Y 7.4%, +40bp in a month

US debt maturity 5.5 years vs India 13.8
